source_snapshot.procedure: Enable Platform First Error Handling, MCA threshold enable/count FFE and Reset After Sync-Flood; unlock CPU through HDT; boot Ubuntu 20.04, RHEL 9.0 or Windows 2022; install AMD RAS tool; list links; then inject error type 1 at hardcoded link 0 for IOD location 0 and CCD location 1. Step labels incorrectly call both injections Correctable.
source_snapshot.criteria: For uncorrectable errors the tool reports PASS and the OS reports within an unspecified timeout; inspect dmesg and the injection report against an unspecified AMD RAS specification.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; tool, HDT and hardware are operator-gated, with generic GMI/XGMI and SEL collection.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION/CHANGED; recognizes uncorrectable risk but does not resolve Correctable step labels, fixed link 0, undefined timeout/recovery outcome or Windows-versus-dmesg evidence.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Appropriately blocks autonomous injection but generic logs cannot prove UCE source, location, severity or bounded recovery.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Adds owner gating and recovery yet assumes the conflicting step labels and incomplete PASS oracle can be resolved during execution.
historical_reviews.related_cases: Row 38 is the separate CE variant using errortype 0. This row's errortype 1 must retain distinct uncorrectable behavior and must not inherit CE acceptance.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Destructive UCE coverage requires exact target, severity, expected reset/sync-flood behavior, abort and independent recovery; copied labels cannot be silently corrected.

original_test_intent: Verify uncorrectable GMI3 handling independently at approved IOD and CCD locations, including attributable error reporting, the project-defined containment or reset response and complete post-event fabric/system recovery.
original_method: Map physical GMI topology from enumeration; preserve CPU/firmware/BIOS/HDT/tool/OS baseline; resolve the Correctable labels versus errortype 1 and approve expected UCE severity, reset/sync-flood policy and recovery deadlines; perform one supervised IOD UCE and, only after full recovery and separate approval, one CCD UCE; correlate tool, MCA/APEI or WHEA, BMC/UEFI, console and link-health evidence; restore all state without automatic retry.
manual_activity: A qualified FAE resolves the UCE semantics and expected containment, provisions HDT and the licensed AMD tool, maps the GMI fabric, performs at most one approved location injection per recovered checkpoint, owns OOB recovery and restores BIOS/HDT state.
required_inputs: Decision that errortype 1 is authoritative UCE despite both procedure labels saying Correctable
CPU/platform link-to-IOD/CCD topology and required link coverage
AMD tool/spec version/hash/license plus linktraffic 1 and errortype 1 semantics
Expected UCE severity, MCA disposition, sync-flood/reset/crash containment and maximum recovery times
Separate Linux MCA/APEI/dmesg and Windows WHEA/console plus BMC/UEFI oracle
BIOS FFE deviation rationale, original settings, backup, OOB recovery, abort and restoration plan
safety_requirements: Isolated non-production SUT, preserved data, independent OOB console and power/reimage recovery
Do not inject until the Correctable labels, UCE severity and expected reset/sync-flood response are resolved
Never assume enumerated link 0; bind the approved physical target and quiesce dependencies
One UCE only per approval; do not proceed to the second location until the first is fully recovered and reviewed
Abort on wrong target/severity, error storm, unexpected reset, lost console/link or failed recovery; no automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate provenance, topology, exact severity/containment oracle and recovery readiness
Collect read-only baseline, tool/console/OS/BMC/UEFI transcript and post-recovery link/system health
Do not unlock HDT, change BIOS, select target, inject UCE, power-cycle/reimage, repeat or determine DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Resolve the Correctable step-label conflict and approve UCE semantics
Approve physical target, package, BIOS values and one-shot sequence
Define deterministic containment, evidence, timeout and recovery for IOD and CCD
Restore the SUT and decide PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Generic GMI/XGMI grep plus SEL tail does not prove an uncorrectable event's physical source or distinguish expected containment from a dangerous escalation; dmesg does not apply to Windows.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After formal UCE approval, use the enumerated physical mapping and execute one literal errortype-1 command for only the approved IOD or CCD location, preserving console and recovery evidence before any separately approved second checkpoint.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Both location commands, linktraffic 1, errortype 1, BIOS controls, supported OS list and 30/20-minute estimates are preserved; the Correctable labels, link 0 and timeout require resolution.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat each IOD/CCD UCE as a separate destructive checkpoint with a mapped target, predicted containment/reset behavior, continuous OOB observation and verified recovery before further action.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds conflict resolution, topology binding, deterministic UCE disposition, OS-specific evidence, hard timeout/abort, serialized checkpoints and restoration.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A tool PASS is injector status, not proof that the intended fabric location handled an uncorrectable event correctly; an uncontrolled crash cannot be assumed to pass.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: UCE can trigger sync flood, fatal machine check, reset, persistent link failure or inaccessible host; recovery itself may require authorized power or reimage action.

project_override_considerations: If link 0 is project-fixed, document its IOD/CCD mapping and scope. If the procedure intended correctable injection, errortype 1 and the Uncorrectable title/criteria require source correction rather than review-layer reinterpretation.
expected_evidence: Approved label/UCE decision, physical topology and tool/spec provenance
BIOS/HDT before, target and restored values plus continuous OOB console
Separate IOD or CCD full command transcript and exact UCE MCA/APEI/WHEA/BMC/UEFI signature
Expected versus observed sync-flood/reset/crash/link behavior and bounded recovery timeline
Post-recovery link/device/system integrity, injector closeout and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The case title, Criteria and errortype 1 say Uncorrectable, but both procedure steps say Correctable. It also enumerates topology then hardcodes link 0, leaves timeout and expected UCE containment undefined, and lists Windows while requiring dmesg. These contradictions directly affect destructive severity and PASS/FAIL interpretation.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The intended GMI3 UCE locations and literal commands are visible. Engineering can resolve the copied labels, topology and containment oracle, so static review completes while execution is strictly gated.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 39 Wistron-System RAS-00759-V003: confirm errortype=1 uncorrectable coverage despite both IOD/CCD steps saying Correctable; approve CPU/platform GMI link-to-location map and link coverage, AMD tool/spec version/hash/license and linktraffic semantics, expected UCE severity plus sync-flood/reset/crash containment and timeout, Linux versus Windows and BMC/UEFI evidence, BIOS FFE deviation, serialized one-shot aborts, OOB recovery and restoration.

review_improvement: Makes the severity-label contradiction explicit and replaces an unsafe generic PASS concept with separately contained, attributable IOD and CCD UCE checkpoints and recovery proof.
independent_technical_reasoning: In fault injection, a copied Correctable label is safety-critical because the numeric errortype selects behavior that may reset or crash the fabric. Tool PASS can mean the request was accepted even when the DUT response is wrong. Therefore the physical link, error severity, expected containment and recovery deadline must be decided before one injection. The second location cannot follow automatically after a disruptive first event, and Windows requires WHEA/console evidence rather than dmesg. These are resolvable execution prerequisites, not a reason to discard the case.
